meta.titre: Free and Open Source Software: freedoms, licences and a school lab decision
meta.sous_theme: Open source licences versus proprietary software

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A cyber cafe owner in Buea must equip ten computers. Each licence for a well-known paid operating system adds to the bill, while another system can be downloaded, studied and installed without paying a licence fee. Many schools and small businesses in Cameroon choose this second kind of software. The GCE asks what free and open source software means, how it differs from proprietary software, and what advantages it brings to a computer laboratory.

items: Software is a set of programs that runs on a computer.
An operating system manages the hardware and other programs.
A program is first written as source code by a programmer.

sections.titre: Free and open source software and proprietary software
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Source code

**Source code** is the program as written by the programmer in a programming language. Users run the compiled version, but only someone with the source code can read how the program works and change it.

### Free and open source software (FOSS)

**Free and open source software** is software whose source code is made available, and whose licence gives users the freedom to:

* run the program for any purpose;
* study how it works and **modify** the source code;
* **redistribute** copies;
* share their modified versions.

"Free" refers to **freedom**, not only to price: much FOSS costs nothing, but the key point is the freedom to use and change it. Examples are the Linux operating system, the LibreOffice package, the Firefox browser, the GIMP image editor and the VLC media player.

### Proprietary software

**Proprietary (closed source) software** belongs to the company that made it. The source code is kept secret, users buy a licence, and copying, changing or sharing it is forbidden by that licence. Examples are Windows and Microsoft Office.

### Comparison

| Point | FOSS | Proprietary |
|---|---|---|
| Source code | Available | Secret |
| Cost | Usually no licence fee | Licence fee |
| Changes by the user | Allowed | Not allowed |
| Support | Community, forums, optional paid support | Supplied by the owner |
| Vendor dependence | Low | High |

### Advantages and drawbacks

Advantages of FOSS: lower cost, ability to adapt the program, many people can inspect the code and report faults, no dependence on one company, legal copying for every machine. Drawbacks: support may be uneven, users may need time to learn it, and some commercial programs are not available.

variantes.nom: Explaining the effect of a change in a lab
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for the advantages of changes made by a technician.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name the change, state what it does, then give the benefit. Open source operating system: no licence fee and freedom to adapt. More RAM: more programs can be held in memory at once, so the computer runs faster with less swapping to disk. UPS (uninterruptible power supply): a battery unit that keeps the computer running when mains power fails, so work is saved and shut down safely, and it protects against sudden power loss.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to suggest more changes.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give practical, different improvements: install antivirus software, use a faster hard disk or a solid state drive, update the software and drivers, add a surge protector, clean the machines regularly, or upgrade the processor.

sections.enonce_markdown: A secondary school in Ngaoundere plans to replace the paid operating system on its 10 lab computers with an open source one. A licence costs 45,000 FCFA per computer (an invented price), and training the teacher costs 60,000 FCFA. (a) Define open source software. (b) Calculate the net saving. (c) Give one possible drawback.

etapes.justification: The definition identifies the source code and the freedoms.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Open source software is software whose source code is available so that users may study, modify and redistribute it.

etapes.justification: Ten computers each need one licence.
Training is a new cost the school will pay.
A balanced answer shows the limits.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Staff and pupils must learn a new system, and some paid programs may not run on it.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Open source software has available source code that users may study, modify and share. The net saving is 390,000 FCFA. A drawback is the time needed to learn the new system.**

items.erreur_markdown: "Free software means software that costs nothing."
items.pourquoi_faux: In FOSS, free refers to freedom to use, study, change and share. Some FOSS may be sold, and some zero-cost software is not open.
items.correction_markdown: Free and open source software gives users freedoms and access to the source code.

items.erreur_markdown: "Open source software can be copied and sold as your own program."
items.pourquoi_faux: It is still covered by a licence, which sets conditions such as keeping the credits and the same freedoms.

items.erreur_markdown: "A UPS makes the computer run faster."
items.pourquoi_faux: A UPS supplies battery power during an outage; speed depends on the processor and RAM.
items.correction_markdown: A UPS keeps the computer running briefly and protects against power cuts, so data is not lost.

items.pourquoi_faux: The abbreviation stands for a different phrase.

items.enonce_markdown: State two features of free and open source software.
items.solution_markdown: Any two: the source code is available; users may modify it; users may redistribute copies; it usually has no licence fee; it is supported by a community. **Award 1 mark per feature.**

items.enonce_markdown: A cyber cafe in Buea has 8 computers. A proprietary licence costs 38,000 FCFA per computer (an invented price). The owner chooses an open source system with no licence fee, but pays 50,000 FCFA for installation. Calculate the saving.
items.solution_markdown: Licences avoided: 8 x 38000 = 304000 FCFA. Installation cost: 50000 FCFA. Saving = 304000 - 50000 = **254,000 FCFA**.

items.enonce_markdown: Discuss whether a school should choose free and open source software instead of proprietary software. Give two advantages and two drawbacks, then say what a UPS adds to the lab.
items.solution_markdown: Advantages (two): no or low licence fees; the school can adapt the software and is not tied to one company; many people check the code; copies may be installed on every machine legally. Drawbacks (two): support depends on the community unless paid for; staff and pupils must learn it; some commercial programs do not run on it. UPS: Uninterruptible Power Supply, a battery unit that keeps computers on during a power cut so that work can be saved and the machines shut down safely. **Conclusion: FOSS is usually a good choice for a school with a small budget, if staff are trained.**

items_markdown: FOSS has available source code and gives the freedom to run, study, modify and share the software.
"Free" means freedom, not only price; examples are Linux, LibreOffice, Firefox, GIMP and VLC.
Proprietary software keeps its source code secret and is sold under a restrictive licence.
Advantages of FOSS: low cost, adaptability, many reviewers, no dependence on one vendor; drawbacks: uneven support and learning time.
More RAM lets more programs run at once; a UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) protects against power cuts.
